title: Bienvenue dans notre école!
oneGoal: Students will identify their school as a special place and express feelings about being part of the school community
decisionPoints: How familiar are students with their school building?
What level of emotional support do students need for school comfort?
Should we focus on building tour or classroom exploration first?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes school as a safe, welcoming community where everyone belongs
realWorldConnection: Every person belongs to communities like school, family, and neighborhood

title: Je suis un élève
oneGoal: Students will understand their identity as students and recognize their rights and responsibilities in school
decisionPoints: Are students ready to discuss responsibilities or should we focus on rights first?
How do we balance individual identity with group belonging?
Should we use role-play or discussion to explore student identity?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by defining what it means to be a student and member of school community
realWorldConnection: Being a student is an important role with special rights and responsibilities

title: Notre salle de classe
oneGoal: Students will explore their classroom space and understand how spaces are organized for learning and community
decisionPoints: Which classroom areas are most meaningful for students to explore?
Should we create a classroom map together or individually?
How do we help students see classroom organization as intentional?
progression: Builds on student identity by connecting to immediate learning environment and spatial awareness
realWorldConnection: All learning spaces are designed to help people work, learn, and be together

title: Les espaces de notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify different school spaces and understand how each space serves the school community
decisionPoints: Which school spaces are most important for students to understand first?
Should we take a walking tour or use photos and maps?
How do we connect spaces to activities and community needs?
progression: Expands from classroom to whole school, building spatial understanding and community awareness
realWorldConnection: Different spaces in our community serve different purposes for different people

title: Notre directeur et secrétaire
oneGoal: Students will understand the roles of principal and secretary in supporting the school community
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with meeting school authority figures?
Should we visit the office or invite guests to our classroom?
How do we present authority as helpful rather than intimidating?
progression: Introduces school leadership roles and how different people contribute to school community
realWorldConnection: Every community has leaders who help organize and support everyone

title: Nos enseignants et aide-enseignants
oneGoal: Students will recognize teaching roles and understand how educators support student learning and growth
decisionPoints: How do we help students see teachers as people with feelings and needs?
Should we interview teachers or observe them in action?
How do we connect teaching to students' own helping experiences?
progression: Builds on leadership roles by focusing on daily support people and learning relationships
realWorldConnection: Teachers and helpers exist in many community settings, not just schools

title: Le concierge et la cuisine
oneGoal: Students will appreciate support staff roles and understand how everyone contributes to school community
decisionPoints: How do we highlight the importance of support roles without stereotyping?
Should we observe work in action or have conversations with staff?
How do we connect support work to students' own helping at home?
progression: Expands understanding of community roles beyond education to essential support services
realWorldConnection: Every community depends on people who maintain spaces and provide services

title: Les règles de notre école
oneGoal: Students will understand school rules as community agreements that help everyone feel safe and included
decisionPoints: Are students ready to discuss rule purposes or should we focus on examples first?
Should we create new class rules or explore existing school rules?
How do we frame rules as helpful rather than restrictive?
progression: Connects community roles to community agreements and shared responsibility for safety
realWorldConnection: All communities have agreements that help people live and work together safely

title: Comment nous résolvons les problèmes
oneGoal: Students will practice conflict resolution and understand how to seek help when problems arise
decisionPoints: What types of conflicts are most relevant to students' experience?
Should we role-play solutions or discuss real classroom situations?
How do we balance independent problem-solving with seeking adult help?
progression: Builds on rules and safety by providing practical tools for community problem-solving
realWorldConnection: Learning to solve problems peacefully helps in all relationships and communities

title: Nos traditions scolaires
oneGoal: Students will explore school traditions and understand how shared experiences build community identity
decisionPoints: Which school traditions are most meaningful for Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on current year traditions or school history?
How do we include diverse cultural perspectives in tradition discussions?
progression: Shifts from rules and problems to positive community building through shared experiences
realWorldConnection: Traditions help communities remember their values and celebrate together

title: Ma carte de l'école
oneGoal: Students will create simple maps of school spaces and understand how maps help us navigate community spaces
decisionPoints: Are students ready for bird's-eye view mapping or should we use floor-level perspective?
Should maps focus on favorite spaces or all school areas?
How do we balance accuracy with creative expression in map-making?
progression: Combines spatial awareness with geographic skills while reinforcing school community knowledge
realWorldConnection: Maps help us understand and navigate all the communities we belong to

title: Interview avec le personnel
oneGoal: Students will conduct simple interviews with school staff to understand their roles and contributions
decisionPoints: Which staff members would be most comfortable and engaging for student interviews?
Should interviews be structured with prepared questions or more conversational?
How do we prepare students for respectful questioning and listening?
progression: Builds on role understanding by adding direct communication and inquiry skills
realWorldConnection: Asking questions and listening to answers helps us understand our community better

title: Les besoins de notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify school community needs and understand how needs are met through cooperation
decisionPoints: How do we help students distinguish between wants and needs in school context?
Should we focus on material needs or emotional/social needs first?
How do we connect school needs to students' ability to contribute solutions?
progression: Shifts from understanding existing community to thinking about improvement and contribution
realWorldConnection: All communities have needs that are met when people work together

title: Comment nous aidons notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can contribute to school community and take action to help
decisionPoints: What level of responsibility are students ready to take on?
Should we focus on individual contributions or group projects?
How do we ensure helping feels joyful rather than burdensome?
progression: Builds on needs identification by empowering students as active community contributors
realWorldConnection: Everyone, including children, can make important contributions to their communities

title: Notre école dans le quartier
oneGoal: Students will understand their school's place in the larger neighborhood community
decisionPoints: How familiar are students with the area around their school?
Should we explore through windows, walks, or maps and photos?
How do we connect school community to broader community relationships?
progression: Expands community understanding beyond school walls to neighborhood connections
realWorldConnection: Schools are part of larger communities with connections to many other places and people

title: Les écoles d'hier et d'aujourd'hui
oneGoal: Students will compare past and present schools and understand how communities change over time
decisionPoints: What aspects of school history will be most interesting and accessible to Grade 1s?
Should we use photos, artifacts, or stories from older community members?
How do we help students see both continuity and change in school communities?
progression: Adds temporal perspective to spatial and social understanding of school community
realWorldConnection: All communities have histories that help us understand how they became what they are today

title: Créer ensemble un projet d'école
oneGoal: Students will collaborate on a project that improves their school community
decisionPoints: What type of project would be meaningful and achievable for Grade 1 students?
Should the project focus on classroom, school, or neighborhood improvement?
How do we balance individual creativity with collaborative decision-making?
progression: Synthesizes learning into concrete action that demonstrates community contribution
realWorldConnection: Working together on projects is how communities solve problems and create positive changes

title: Présenter notre école
oneGoal: Students will share their school community knowledge with others and practice being school ambassadors
decisionPoints: Who would be the best audience for student presentations about their school?
Should presentations be formal or conversational, individual or group?
How do we help students feel confident representing their school community?
progression: Transforms students from community learners to community teachers and representatives
realWorldConnection: Being able to describe and represent our communities helps others understand and appreciate them

title: Notre célébration scolaire
oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a celebration that honors their school community
decisionPoints: What format of celebration would best honor the diverse contributions in school community?
Should celebration focus on students, staff, or the whole school community?
How do we ensure celebration includes and values everyone's contributions?
progression: Culminates learning with joy and appreciation for school community relationships
realWorldConnection: Celebrations help communities appreciate their shared experiences and values

title: Moi, élève et citoyen
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their growth as school community members and set goals for continued contribution
decisionPoints: How do we help students see their learning journey and growth over the unit?
Should reflection focus on personal growth or community contribution?
How do we help students set realistic goals for continued school citizenship?
progression: Concludes unit by connecting school citizenship to broader community membership and future growth
realWorldConnection: Being a good community member is a lifelong journey of learning, contributing, and growing
